clue.text: See 9
Receivers receiving setter's payment, initially, in coins

indicators.note: one thing receiving another takes it in, so the second group of letters goes inside the first

parts.note: a receiver of stolen goods is a fence
the setter says 'I have', shortened to I'VE

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of payment

explanation.surface: Handlers of stolen goods take the compiler's fee in coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receivers' suggests radios or tax officials; here it is the slang for dealers in stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Fivepences are the small British coins worth five pence each, so the plural names pieces of currency.

clue.text: Bulb in lift lifted in house

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, so the reversed letters go inside the house

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to doff a hat is to lift it

explanation.surface: A light bulb in a lift is raised up through a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' reads as a light bulb, but it is the flower that grows from one. The house is the Dáil, the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A daffodil grows from a bulb, so the flower is named by the plant organ it springs from.

clue.text: States circumvented by hasty retreat of gay character

indicators.note: something circumvented by another is surrounded by it, so States sits within the other letters
a retreat is a going back, so the word for hasty is read backwards

parts.note: rash means hasty
US is the United States

explanation.surface: The United States are outflanked by a gay figure's sudden withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gay' is used in its old sense of dashing and carefree.
explanation.definitionFit: Hussars, the light cavalry, were proverbially dashing, flamboyant soldiers, hence a 'gay' (jaunty) character in the old sense.

clue.text: Terrorist (cyber-criminal) embracing leaders of Islamic jihad

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the picked letters go inside the cyber-criminal

parts.note: a hacker breaks into computer systems

indicators.note: leaders are the first letters of Islamic and jihad

explanation.surface: A terrorist who is also an online criminal is drawn in by Islamist militant leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A hijacker seizes a vehicle or aircraft by force, an act of terrorism.

clue.text: Pasquale, perhaps, cross-culturally cross-dressing, cold and dry

indicators.note: Pasquale is dressed in the garment, so his letters go inside it

parts.note: the garment worn across cultures is the sari, the Indian woman's dress
Don Pasquale is the title character of Donizetti's opera, so Pasquale is an example of a don
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: An opera character dresses in another culture's women's clothes, and stays cold and dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Pasquale is Donizetti's opera; a man in a sari, a woman's dress from another culture, is cross-dressing cross-culturally. Pasquale is also a Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is wry and mocking, which is what a sardonic remark is.

clue.text: Mutant 2 transmuted metal

indicators.note: transmuted means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: two in Roman numerals is II

explanation.surface: A second mutant has been changed into metal, like a comic-book superhero.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a light, strong element used in aircraft and implants.

clue.text: One-trick artist's creation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A one-trick pony of a painter has made something.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a religious painting, a work made by an artist.

clue.text: Yen to interrupt thousandth tall tale?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so the letter for yen goes inside the other letters

parts.note: thousandth is written in figures-and-letters style as Mth, with M the Roman thousand
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A craving breaks in on the thousandth telling of an exaggerated story.
explanation.walkthrough: Just as 4th is written with TH, 'thousandth' becomes M (Roman 1000) plus TH. The question mark flags that a myth is only loosely a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a fabulous traditional story, which can be compared to an exaggerated yarn.

clue.text: Inquisitor wrecked Manx army jeep

indicators.note: a wrecked jeep is smashed apart, so the letters of these three words are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A military jeep from the Isle of Man lies smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: JEREMY PAXMAN is a British broadcaster famous for his relentless, hectoring interviews on Newsnight and as quizmaster of University Challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcaster's fierce interrogation of politicians earned him a reputation as television's grand interrogator.

clue.text: Ecstatic about coiffure for prom

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters go round the hairstyle

parts.note: sent is an old slang word for enraptured
an Afro is a hairstyle

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled about their hairdo for the school dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prom' suggests the school dance, but here it is short for promenade.
explanation.definitionFit: Prom is short for promenade, a walkway along the shore at a seaside town.

clue.text: Monarch caught by his opponent on air

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: on air means broadcast, i.e. spoken out, so the word is replaced by one that sounds like it

parts.note: the Roundheads were the Parliamentarians who fought King Charles I

explanation.surface: A king is captured by his enemy during a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: C (caught) followed by a sound-alike of ROUNDHEAD: the Roundheads were the Parliamentarian side opposing the king in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowned head is a reigning king or queen, someone who wears the crown.

clue.text: Discouragement of French dramatist adopting recipe

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the letter goes inside the dramatist's name

parts.note: Terence was a Roman comic playwright
R is the abbreviation for recipe, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A French playwright is put off by being handed a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterrence is the act of putting people off doing something, a form of dissuasion.

clue.text: Feel bad about turning on gas in beleaguered economic area

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the next piece
turning means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to rue something is to feel bad about it
ozone is a gas

explanation.surface: Someone regrets switching on the gas while in a struggling business region.
explanation.definitionFit: The eurozone, the countries using the euro, was under severe strain in the debt crisis of the time.

clue.text: Kind of ancient Roman people keeping half of 13 confused

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the mixed letters go inside the Roman clan

parts.note: a gens was a Roman clan

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the first half of the answer to 13 down

explanation.surface: A sort of ancient Roman folk held half of a puzzling economic zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' looks like it means 'type of', but 'Kind' is the definition and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous and kind are synonyms for a person who gives freely.

clue.text: Discriminatory fifth-rankers catching seventh note

indicators.note: catching means trapping inside, so the note goes within the other letters

parts.note: celebrities are ranked A-list down to E-list, so fifth-rankers are the E-list
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Low-grade celebrities are caught out in a prejudice against those below them.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist attitude favours a select group and looks down on others, a form of discrimination.

clue.text: Hobby generating unearned income

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pastime or pursuit
second meaning: money paid on savings or loans

explanation.surface: A pastime that brings in money without work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a leisure pursuit and the return paid on invested capital.

clue.text: Eg fungus-scavenger initially multiplied by 20

indicators.note: the first letter V, Roman five, is multiplied by twenty to become C, Roman one hundred

parts.note: a vulture is a scavenging bird

explanation.surface: A fungus-eating creature's numbers are first boosted twentyfold.
explanation.walkthrough: Treat the V in VULTURE as the Roman 5; times 20 it becomes 100, or C.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus grown in a laboratory dish is an example of a culture.

clue.text: Dance mistress and dissolute priest on the job

indicators.note: dissolute means loose-living, so the letters of the word are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: a chore is a job

explanation.surface: A dance teacher and a debauched cleric are at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichore is the Muse of dance in Greek myth, so she presides over the art.

clue.text: 15 circle needing brains to crack this?

indicators.note: brains break into the word, so the letters for brains go inside it

parts.note: this refers to the clue itself
IQ measures intelligence

explanation.surface: An exclusive group needs intelligence to solve this puzzle clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the very thing being solved, the clue. 15 is ELITIST, so the definition is an elitist circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is a small exclusive group, the kind of select circle that keeps others out.

clue.text: Idle, maybe, being possessed of infinite riches

indicators.note: the words possess the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: Laziness can still mean owning boundless wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idle' looks like the lazy adjective; it is Eric Idle of Monty Python.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Idle is a member of Monty Python, so Idle is an example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: Weasel docked in colonnade

indicators.note: an animal's tail is docked by cutting it short, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a stoat is a member of the weasel family

explanation.surface: A weasel with a clipped tail is in a covered walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered walkway lined with columns in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: What Syrinx did in 8? Yielded!

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: in the myth (8 down) Syrinx did a TURN into a REED, so TURN goes in REED
second meaning: produced as a return, as an investment does

explanation.surface: Asking what a nymph did in a myth, and answering that she gave way.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nymph Syrinx escaped Pan by being turned into reeds. Split the answer as RE(TURN)ED: a TURN inside REED.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment that returned a profit yielded it, so the two verbs share the sense of producing a gain.

clue.text: Yob getting hold of New Order's 22 garment

indicators.note: the answer to 22 across means come back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
getting hold of means grasping inside, so the yob holds the other letters

parts.note: an oik is a British word for an uncouth lout
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A lout grabs a returned item of clothing from a new religious order.
explanation.walkthrough: OIK (a lout) holds N and OM to give ONOMIK, and '22' (RETURNED) reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A kimono is a loose Japanese robe, an article of clothing.

clue.text: Unfashionable subject's popular favourites

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the study of Latin and Greek, now less taught
second meaning: well-loved works of lasting appeal

explanation.surface: A subject out of fashion still has its well-loved favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the academic study of ancient Greece and Rome and enduring, much-loved works.

clue.text: Polish writers wanting head of Polish painter

parts.note: to rub is to polish

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Writers from Poland lack a leading Polish artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality; it is the verb, to polish. PENS loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque artist known for large canvases.
